explain.say: Your class votes for their favourite pet. How can you keep track of the votes fast? With tally marks! Look at the board: the bars show the votes for each pet: dog 8, cat 6, bird 4 and fish 3.

explain.say: For each vote, draw one straight line, called a tally mark. For the fifth, draw a line across the other four, like a little gate. That makes a bundle of 5. Dog got 8: one gate of 5 and 3 more lines. Can you draw 8 in tally marks?

faq.q: How do I draw tally marks?
faq.a: Draw one straight line for each thing you count. For the fifth, draw a line across the first four. Then start a new group.
asks: How do I make tally marks?

faq.q: Why is the fifth tally mark drawn across?
faq.a: It bundles the marks into groups of 5, like a gate. Then you can count in fives quickly instead of counting every line.
asks: Why do tally marks have a line across?

faq.a: A tally chart is a table with a list of choices and tally marks beside each one. It helps you count votes or things as they happen, then write the totals.
asks: What does a tally chart show?

faq.q: How many more votes did dog get than fish?
faq.a: Dog got 8 votes and fish got 3. 8 take away 3 is 5, so dog got 5 more votes.
asks: What is the difference between dog and fish?

faq.a: A survey is when you ask people a question and record their answers, like asking everyone their favourite pet. A tally chart is a good way to record a survey.

facts: In a tally, every fifth mark is drawn across the four before it to make a group of 5.
The Ishango bone, found in Central Africa and about 20,000 years old, has notches that may be an early tally.
